Pre-requisite: Engineering Mathematics – I, II (BTAB01001, BTAB02001)
Objectives:
 To provide a set of tools and methods to solve linear algebraic equations and
also to determine the eigen values and eigen vectors
 To inculcate the ability to solve engineering problems using Laplace
transforms of commonly used functions
 To develop ability to solve the problems using concept of Fourier series
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students will be able to
 Solve linear algebraic equations and also to determine the eigen values and
eigen vectors
 Solve engineering problems using Laplace transforms of commonly used
functions
 Solve the problems using concept of Fourier series
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Matrices:
Linear dependence and independence of rows and columns of a
matrix over real field, System of linear homogeneous and non-
homogeneous equations, Characteristic equation, Eigen values   12
and Eigen vectors of a square matrix, Cayley-Hamilton Theorem,
Similar Matrices, Diagonalization, Functions of a Square Matrix,
Quadratic Forms.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/2
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
2.   Laplace transform
Definition, Laplace transform of 1, e at ,sin at ,cos at ,sinh at ,cosh at , t n
, First shifting theorem, Change of scale property, Evaluation of
Inverse Laplace using partial fraction, Convolution Theorem,
L  t n f ( t )  , L   f ( t )   , L     t f ( u ) du    , L  f n ( t )  , Laplace transforms of   20
   t    0    
Periodic functions, Unit step functions, Second shifting theorem ,
Dirac delta functions and their Laplace Transform, Application to
solve initial and boundary value problems involving ordinary
differential equations.
3.   Fourier Series:
Trigonometric Series, Definition of Periodic function, Dirichlet’s
conditions, Euler’s formulae (Derivation of Fourier coefficients a0,
an, bn is not expected), Fourier series for the interval [  ,  2  ]
and   , [  ,   2 c ] , Function having points of discontinuity, Even   13
and Odd functions, Half range sine and cosine expansions,
Parseval’s   identities,   Orthogonality and   orthonormality,
Expression for a function in a series of orthogonal functions.
Total   45
Note: Proofs of theorems are not expected.

Publishers

Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester :   III
Course :   Surveying-I   Code : BTCI03002
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical Tutorial Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   2   0   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Engineering Mathematics- II (BTAB02001)
Objectives:
 To impart knowledge of the basic surveying and levelling
 To determine the positions of distinctive features of the earth’s surface by
relative distances, heights, directions and angles
 To operate surveying instruments
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Describe the measurement techniques in different types of surveys
 Take measurements for plotting the positions of distinctive features and
carry out calculations from the observations of surveying
 Operate different instruments used in surveying for carrying out basic
surveying and levelling
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Introduction:   08
Definitions, principle, Various types of surveying – based on
methods and instruments, classifications, uses, necessity and use
of various scales and verniers.
Different types of ranging, tapes, chains, Linear measurements,
approximate, direct, optical and electronic methods, Chain
surveying, minor instruments for setting out right angle.
2.   Compass Surveying:   05
Definitions, Principle, Different Types-prismatic, surveyor,
Bearings-whole   circle, reduced, fore and back bearings,
declination, local attraction, plotting of compass survey by
different methods and their corrections, Errors, Precautions.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/4
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Levelling and Contouring:   12
Definitions, technical terms, uses, details of levels such as
dumpy, tilting and auto levelling staff,   Temporary and
permanent adjustments of dumpy and auto level, corrections-
curvature, refraction, combine and sensitiveness, reciprocal
levelling, collimation and rise & fall method, errors, precautions.
Contour – definitions, objectives, contour interval, horizontal
equivalent, uses and characteristics of contour lines, methods of
plotting contours, direct and indirect methods of contouring,
Contour gradient.
4.   Computation of Area and Volume:   05
Area of a irregular figure by Trapezoidal rule, Mid-ordinate rule,
average- ordinate rule, Simpson’s rule, various coordinate
methods, planimeter.
Computation of volume by trapezoidal and prismoidal formula.
5.   Theodolite Surveying:   10
Objective, various parts of transit theodolite, technical terms,
temporary and permanent adjustments of a transit, measuring
horizontal and vertical angles, methods of repetition and
reiteration, computation of latitude and departure, balancing of
traverse by Bow-Ditch’s transit rule, third rule and modified
transit rules, missing data problems, Precautions in using
theodolite, errors in theodolite survey, use of latitude and
departure for area calculation, Gales traverse table.
6.   Plane Table Surveying:   05
Definitions, uses and advantages, Different methods of plane
table surveying, Two point problem, Errors in plane table survey,
use of telescopic alidade.
Total   45
Text Book:
1. Kanetkar and Kulkarni (2011),“Surveying and Levelling”, Vol I and II, Pune
Vidyarthi Griha, Pune
2. N. N. Basak (2010),“Surveying and Levelling”, Tata McGraw Hill
Reference Books:
1. Dr. K.R. Arora (2009), “ Surveying “ vol.I, II & III”, Standard Book House, New
Delhi
2. Dr. B.C. Punmia, Ashok K. Jain, Arun K. Jain (2005), “Surveying Vol. - I, II &
III”, Laxmi Publications (P) Ltd., New Delhi
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/5
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
Term Work:
Term work should consists of the following
1. Minimum five assignments covering the prescribed syllabus.
2. Report of minimum six experiments performed from the list given below.
List of Experiments
1. Introduction to measuring instruments
2. Chain Survey- chain and cross staff survey
3. Compass survey
4. Levelling - By height of instrument and rise & fall method
5. Theodolite - Measurement of horizontal and vertical angle
6. Theodolite traversing
7. Plane table surveying
8. Various minor instruments used in survey engineering
9. Use of planimeter for measuring area of irregular figures
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/6
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester :   III
Course :   Strength of Materials   Code : BTCI03003
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical Tutorial Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   2   0   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Engineering Mechanics - I (BTAB01005)
Engineering Mechanics – II (BTAB02005)
Objectives:
 To impart knowledge of the behaviour of the deformable bodies subjected to
different types of loads
 To determine the failure criteria when body is subjected to various stresses
 To understand the concept of deformations
 To identify the different tests to be performed on metals
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Calculate the stresses produced in the deformable bodies
 Determine the failure criteria when body is subjected to various stresses
 Evaluate the deformations of the various determinate beams
 Carry out testing of different metals and determine the material properties
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Axial force, shear force and bending moment in beams:   07
Axial force, shear force & bending moment diagrams for
statically determinate beams including beams with internal
hinges for different types of loading, relationships between rate
of loading, shear force and bending moment.
2.   Stress & strain:   06
Stress, yield stress, ultimate stress, shear stress, factor of safety,
strain, modulus of elasticity (E), modulus of rigidity (G), bulk
modulus (K), Poisson’s ratio, relationship between elastic
constants, bars of varying sections, stresses in composite section,
temperature stresses
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/7
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Simple theory of bending:   06
Flexure formula for beam, simple problems involving the
application of flexure formula, section modulus, moment of
resistance of a section, flitched/ composite beams.
4.   Shear stress in beams:   04
Distribution of shear stress across plane sections used commonly
for beams, shear connectors.
5.   Simple theory of torsion:   04
Torsion of circular shafts - solid and hollow, stresses and strains
in shaft when transmitting power
6.   Bending moment combined with axial loads:   04
Application to members subjected to eccentric loads, core of the
section. Problems on chimneys, retaining walls, etc.
7.   Principal stresses:   07
General equations for transformation of stress, principles planes
and principal stresses, maximum shear stress, determination
using Mohr’s circle.
8.   Thin cylindrical and spherical shells:   03
Stresses and strains in thin cylindrical and spherical shells
subjected to internal pressure
9.   Deflections of beams:   04
Deflection of cantilever, simply supported and overhanging
beams for different types of loadings using double integration
method and Macaulay’s method.
Total   45
Text Book:
1. James M. Gere, Barry J. Goodno (2012), “Mechanics of Materials – SI
Edition”, Cengage Learning
Reference Books:
1. Andrew Pytel, Jaan Kiusalaas (2011), “Mechanics of Materials – Second
Edition”, Cengage Learning
2. Ferdinand P. Beer, E. Russell Johnston Jr., John T. DeWolf (2008), “Mechanics
of Materials – Third Edition”, Tata McGraw Hill
3. William Nash, Merle Potter (2010), “Schaum's Outline of Strength of
Materials, Fifth Edition”, McGraw Hill Professional
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/8
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
Term Work:
Term work should consists of the following
1. Minimum five assignments covering the prescribed syllabus
2. Report of minimum six experiments performed in the laboratory from the list
given below:-
List of Experiments:-
1. Tension test on mild steel rod.
2. Tension test on tor steel rod
3. Bend and re-bend test on bars
4. Transverse test on cast iron specimen.
5. Shear test on metal specimens.
6. Torsion test on mild steel / cast iron specimen.
7. Load deflection test on metal specimens.
8. Brinell hardness test on metal specimens.
9. Rockwell hardness test on metal specimens.
10. Charpy impact test on metal specimens
11. Izod impact test on metal specimens.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/9
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester :   III
Course :   Building Materials and Construction   Code : BTCI03004
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical   Tutorial   Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   0   2   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Engineering Physics (BTAB01002)
Engineering Chemistry (BTAB02002)
Objectives:
 To impart the knowledge of various building materials
 To know the various building construction processes
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Differentiate various building materials in terms of their types, properties,
defects, processes and uses
 Describe various building construction processes
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Requirements of Building Materials and Products: Functional,   8
Aesthetical And Economical.
Study of Properties of Materials: Physical, Mechanical, Chemical,
Biological and other Engineering Properties.
Stone: Types, Properties, Testing, Qualities of Good Stones, Quarrying
(definition, important considerations, tools, machines, process),
Surface Finishing, Preservative Treatments.
Binder   material:   Lime, Cement:   Physical   Properties and
Manufacturing Process, Plaster of Paris, Type and their uses.
2.   Timber: general, classification, Structure, Processing, Felling,   7
Seasoning, Conversion, defects in timber, Qualities of good
timber, strength of timber, decay of timber, preservative
treatments and wood composites
3.   Paints: Characteristics of Good Paints, objective of painting,   4
Constituents, Types, Process of Painting, Failure of Paints, Defects in
Painting.
Varnishes: Characteristics of ideal varnish, ingredients, types, process,
distempering (properties, ingredients, process), white washing and
colourwashing (properties, ingredients, process).
4.   Glass: Raw Material, Manufacturing Process, Types and Uses   5
Metal and alloys: Ferrous and Non Ferrous Metals and Alloys,
Aluminum, Tin , Zinc, Nickel, (Types Properties and Uses) and Anti-
Corrosive Treatment
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/10
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
5.   Structural clay products: Bricks, Roofing Tiles, Ceramic Tiles, (Raw   9
Materials And Manufacturing Process, Properties, Types, Uses).
Concrete Blocks, Flooring Tiles, Paver Blocks (Raw Materials And
Manufacturing Process, Properties, Types, Uses)
Mortar And Concrete: Ingredients, Types, Preparation And Uses
Miscellaneous materials: Asbestos, Ashpalt, Plastic, Bitumen,
Flyash, Rubber (Properties, Uses and Types).
6.   Types of structures: framed, load bearing and composite structures.   12
Suitability and economic aspects of each type and components of
each type.
Masonry construction: Classification and Bonding in stone, brick
and concrete blocks.
Floors and roofs: Types of floors, floor finishes and suitability.
Types of roofs, wooden and steel trusses, roof coverings and
drainage
Formwork: materials used, design considerations, slip form
shuttering, centering and staging, scaffolding
Staircase: types, size and location, layout, design considerations
Masonry finishes: Pointing, Plastering and Painting
Total   45
Text Books:
1. S. K. Duggal (2009), “Building Materials”, New Age International
Reference Books:
1. P.C. Varghese (2007), “Building Construction”, PHI Leaning Pvt. Ltd.
2. P.C. Varghese (2005), “Building Materials”, PHI Leaning Pvt. Ltd.
3. S.C. Rangawala (2012), “Engineering Materials", Charotar Publishing House
Pvt. Ltd.
4. S.C. Rangawala (2009), “Building Construction", Charotar Publishing House
Pvt. Ltd.
Term Work:
Term work should consists of
1. Minimum five assignments covering the prescribed syllabus
2. Detailed sketches of various components of buildings
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/11
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester :   III
Course :   Engineering Geology   Code : BTCI03005
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical Tutorial Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   0   0   3   50   50
Pre-requisite: Engineering Physics (BTAB01002),
Engineering Chemistry (BTAB02002)
Objectives:
 To impart knowledge of importance of Geology in Civil Engineering
 To impart knowledge of different types of Rocks and their application in
Civil Engineering
 To make students aware of Geological Investigations required for some of
the Civil Engineering Projects
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Explain the relevance of Geology in Civil Engineering
 Differentiate various types of minerals, rocks with their suitability
 Discuss the procedure for geological investigation for some of the Civil
Engineering Projects
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Introduction:   08
Scope of Geology, Brief history of formation of earth and earth
crust, internal constitutions of earth, relationship of geology to
Civil Engineering
Physical Geology: Introduction, Effect of natural agencies ( wind,
running water, sub surface water, lakes, oceans, glaciers,
organisms, volcanoes, earth quakes) taking part in changing the
surface of the earth, Earthquake Belts in India
Structural Geology:
Introduction, Causes of Development of Structures, Structural
Elements - Folds, Faults, Joints, Unconformity, Dip, Strike,
Outcrop Patterns, Outliers and Inliers, Importance of Structural
Elements in Civil Engineering operations.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/12
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
2.   Mineralogy:   10
Introduction, Definition of Mineral and Crystal, Mode of
Formation of Minerals, Common Rock-Forming Minerals and
their Abundance, Different Methods of Study of Minerals,
Significance of   different Physical Properties in Mineral
Identification, Diagnostic Physical Properties.
Study of Common Rock Forming Minerals:
Quartz Family, Feldspar Family, Augite, Hornblende, Biotite,
Muscovite,   Calcite,   (Properties,   Behaviour,   Engineering
Significance), Significance of Clay Minerals (Fundamentals of
process of formation of ore minerals (Coal and Petroleum – Their
Origin and occurrence in India)
3.   Petrology:   11
Introduction, Shell Structure of Earth, Definition of Rocks,
Classification of Rocks, Sequence of Formation of Different
Groups of Rocks, Rock Cycle, Civil Engineering Importance of
Petrology.
Igneous Rocks – Forms of Igneous Rocks- Plutonic & Hypabasal,
Common Igneous Rocks and relation of their Constituent
Minerals, Classification of Igneous Rocks, Structure and Textures,
Suitability of Igneous Rocks for Building and Foundation,
Megascopic   Description of Common Igneous Rock Types,
Descriptive Study of Common Sedimentary Rocks (Sandstone,
Limestone, Shale, Conglomerate, and Breccias)
Sedimentary Rocks – Introduction, Classification of Sedimentary
Rocks, Common Structures and Textures of Sedimentary Rocks,
Descriptive Study of Common Sedimentary Rocks (Granite,
Syenite, Diorite, Dolomite, Gabbro, Pegmatite, Dolerite and
Basalt.
Metamorphic Rocks – Introduction, Metamorphism, Common
Structures and Textures of Metamorphic Rocks, Classification of
Metamorphic Rocks, Descriptive Study of Common Metamorphic
Rocks (Quarzite, Marble, Slate, Thyllite, Gniess, Schist).
4.   Stratigraphy:   08
Principle of stratigraphy and co-relation, geological time scale,
physiographic divisions of India – study of formations occurring
in peninsular India.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/13
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
5.   Ground water:   08
Sources and zones, water table, unconfined and perched, springs,
Factors controlling water bearing capacity of rocks, pervious and
impervious rocks, cone of depression and its use in civil
engineering, Methods of artificial recharge of ground water,
geology of percolation tank.
Geophysical Investigation:
Necessity, Methods of surface and sub surface investigations,
Importance of Electrical Resistivity Method, Seismic Refraction
Method, Preliminary geological investigations, Use of aerial
photographs and satellite imageries in civil engineering projects
Engineering Geology:
Geology of dam sites, reservoirs, roads, bridge sites and tunnels
(broad outlines), Stability of hills slopes, landslides, their causes
and precautions against them
Total   45
Text Books:
1. Singh Parbin (2012), “Engineering and General Geology”, S. K. Kataria and
Sons
Reference Books:
1. K. Mukherjee (2010), “Textbook of Geology”, The World Press Pvt. Ltd.
2. P. C. Varghese (2012), “Engineering Geology for Civil Engineer”, PHI
Learning Private Ltd.
3. N. Chenna Kesavullu (2009), “Textbook of Engineering Geology”, Mac Millan
Publisher India Ltd.
Term Work:
Term work should consists of following
1. Minimum eight assignments covering the prescribed syllabus
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/14
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester :   III
Course :   Fluid Mechanics   Code : BTCI03006
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical Tutorial Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   2   0   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Engineering Mechanics – II (BTAB01005)
Engineering Mathematics – I, II (BTAB01001, BTAB02001)
Objectives:
 To impart knowledge of different properties of fluids
 To inculcate the concept of fluid statics, kinematics and dynamics
 To make students aware of different flow measuring devices
 To introduce the laminar flows and liquids in equilibrium
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Explain the different Properties of fluids
 Differentiate the fluid statics, kinematics and dynamics
 Measure flow using different measuring devices
 Analyze laminar flow and liquids in equilibrium
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Properties of Fluids   05
Mass density, weight density, specific gravity, specific volume,
viscosity, compressibility, bulk modulus, surface tension,
capillary action, vapour pressure, types of fluids, basic concepts.
2.   Fluid Statics   08
Pascal’s Law, Pressure variation in fluid at rest, absolute,
atmospheric, gauge pressure, measurement of pressure, and
hydrostatic forces on plane and curved surfaces. Buoyancy and
flotation: Archimedes’s principle, Metacentre, Metacentric height,
equilibrium of floating and submerged bodies.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/15
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Fluid Kinematics and Dynamics   08
Description of fluid flow: Lagrangian method, Eulerian method,
Streamlines, pathlines, streaklines, classification of fluid flows,
continuity equation, rotational flow, rotation and vorticity,
velocity and stream function. Circulation, flow net. Eular’s
equation, Bernoulli’s theorem, its application to real fluid
4.   Flow measurement   10
Venturimeter, nozzle meter, pitot tube, rotameter.
Orifices: Hydraulic coefficients, small and large orifices, time of
emptying of tank through orifices. Mouthpieces: External,
convergent, Borda’s mouthpiece. Notches and weirs: rectangular,
triangular, Cipolleti weirs, velocity of approach, end contraction
5.   Liquids in relative equilibrium   06
Uniform linear acceleration, liquid container subjected to
constant horizontal and vertical acceleration, constant rotation
with vertical axis.
6.   Laminar flow   08
Reynold’s experiment, Critical velocity, Steady laminar flow
through circular pipes, annulus, parallel plates: stationary and
moving, kinetic correction factor, momentum correction factor,
Dash pot
Total   45
Text Book:
1. Modi P.M. and Seth S.M. (2011), “Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics”, Standard
Book House
Reference Books:
1. Bansal R.K. (2011), “Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics”, Laxmi Publications
2. Subramanaya K., (2008), “Theory and Applications of Fluid Mechanics”, Tata
McGraw Hill
Term Work:
Term work should consists of the following
1. Minimum five assignments covering the prescribed syllabus
2. Report of minimum six experiments performed in the laboratory from the list
given below:-
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM III/16
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
List of Experiments:-
1. Verification of Archemedies principle
2. Verification of Bernoulli’s theorem
3. Calibration of Rotameter
4. Determination of metacentric height
5. Calibration of Orifice
6. Calibration of notches

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester : IV
Course :   Structural Analysis - I   Code : BTCI04003

3   0   2   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Engineering Mechanics –II (BTAB02005)
Strength of Materials (BTCI03003)
Objectives:
 To impart knowledge of the behaviour of different structures subjected to
different types of loads
 To evaluate the internal forces developed in different structures under
various loads
 To determine the failure criteria when body is subjected to various stresses to
study rolling loads and its effect on the structures
 To understand the plotting of influence line diagrams for beams
 To resolve the arches and cables and suspension bridges subjected to loads
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Determine the internal forces developed in various structures subjected to
various loads
 Calculate the deformations in various structures subjected to various loads
 Evaluate stresses for rolling loads and its effect on the structures
 Plot the influence lines diagrams for beams
 Analyse the arches and cables and suspension bridges subjected to loads
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Axial force, shear force and bending moment in frames:   06
Axial force, shear force and bending moment diagrams for
statically determinate frames with and without internal hinges
2.   General theorems:   04
Theorems relating to elastic structures, principle of virtual work.
Strain energy in elastic structures, stresses due to axial load &
impact load. Complementary energy, Castigliano’s theorem,
Betti’s and Maxwell’s reciprocal theorems, principle of
superposition
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM IV/7
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Deflection of statically determinate structures:   10
Deflection of cantilevers, simply supported and overhanging
beams for different types of loadings using following methods:
Moment area method, Conjugate beam, Principle of virtual work
(unit load method) and Castigliano’s theorem. Deflection of
determinate pin jointed and rigid jointed frames by principle of
virtual work (unit load method) and Castigliano’s theorem.
4.   Influence lines for statically determinate structures:   08
Influence lines for cantilevers, simply supported, overhanging
beams and pin jointed truss, criteria for maximum shear force
and bending moment at a section, absolute maximum shear force
and bending moment under moving loads (udl and series of
point loads) for simply supported beams.
5.   Three hinged arch:   06
Determination of normal thrust, radial shear force and bending
moment for three hinged parabolic and segmental arches.
6.   Cables and suspension bridges:   06
Simple suspension cable, minimum and maximum tensions in
the cable supported at same and at different levels, anchor cable,
cable supports, suspension cable with three hinged stiffening
girder, shear force and bending moments at any section of the
stiffening girder.
7.   Columns and Struts:   05
Short and long/slender columns, Concept of buckling in slender
columns subjected to axial loads, Euler’s and Rankine’s design
formulae for columns with different support conditions.
Total   45

Objectives:

 To acquire knowledge of flow networks
 To get acquainted with the dimensional analysis and ideal fluid flow
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Explain the flow through pipes and open channels
 Analyze the flow network
 Discuss the dimensional analysis and ideal flow
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Flow Through Pipes:   12
Loss of head through pipes, Darcy Weisbach equation, minor
losses, total energy line, hydraulic energy line, pipes in series,
pipes in parallel, equivalent pipes, siphons, power transmission
through pipes, power transmission through nozzles.
2.   Pipe Network:   08
Hardy cross method, branching of pipes, three reservoir problem,
water hammer in pipes.
3.   Flow Through Open Channel:   06
Classification of channels, Uniform flow, Chezy’s formula,
Manning’s formula, Prismatic and non-prismatic channels,
hyraulically efficient channel cross-section, Velocity distribution
in open channels, pressure distribution in open channels,
Applications of Bernoulli’s equation to open channel flow.
4.   Non - Uniform Open Channel Flow: Specific energy and   06
discharge curve, applications of specific energy, Momentum
principle, application to open channel flow, specific force, small
waves and surges in open channels, gradually varied flow, control
section, hydraulic jump, location of hydraulic jump.

SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
5.   Dimensional Analysis:   08
Dimensional homogeneity, Buckingham’s π theorem, Rayleigh’s
method, dimensionless groups, similitude, model studies,
distorted & undistorted models.
6.   Ideal Fluid Flow:   05
Uniform flow, source and sink, free vortex flow, superimposed
flow, doublet, flow past half bodies, Rankine’s body and cylinder
only.
Total   45

slopes, types of slope failures, wedge failure, Swedish circle method,
friction circle method, stability numbers and charts.
2. Lateral Earth Pressure Theories   08
Introduction: applications of earth pressure theories, different types
of earth pressures - at rest, active and passive pressures, Rankine’s
earth pressure theory: Rankine’s earth pressure theory, active earth
pressure and passive earth pressure for horizontal and inclined
backfill,Earth Pressure for cohesionless and cohesive soils, Coulomb’s
wedge theory: Coulomb’s active pressure in cohesionless soils,
expression for active pressure, Coulomb’s passive earth pressure.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/2
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3. Bearing capacity of shallow foundations   12
Definitions of ultimate bearing capacity, gross, net and safe pressures,
allowable bearing pressure, types of shallow foundations, modes of
failures, Terzaghi’s Bearing capacity Theory, concept behind
derivation of equation, general bearing capacity equation, bearing
capacity equations for square and circular footings, factors
influencing bearing capacity, performance of footings in different
soils, Vesic’s chart, ultimate bearing capacity in case of local shear
failure.
Plate load test in detail with reference to IS 1888 and its applications
and estimation of settlements, bearing capacity based on standard
penetration test.
4. Axially loaded pile foundations   08
Introduction to pile foundations, necessity of pile foundation,
classification of piles, construction methods of bored piles, concrete
bored piles, driven cast in-situ piles, Pile capacity based on static
analysis, piles in sand, piles in clay, dynamic methods and their
limitations, in-situ penetration tests and pile load test as per IS 2911
specifications, negative skin friction, Pile groups, ultimate capacity of
groups, settlement of pile groups in sand and in clays as per IS 2911
and critical depth method.
5. Underground conduits   04
Classes of underground conduits, load on a ditch conduit, settlement
ratio, ditch condition and projection condition, imperfect ditch
conduit.
6. BracedCuts   04
Lateral Earth Pressure Distribution, Apparent pressure diagrams,
deep cuts in sand, saturated clay, Bjerrum and Eide Method of
Analysis
7. Reinforced soil   03
The mechanism, reinforcement (elements), reinforced-soil interaction,
applications, reinforced soil embankments, simple problems.
Total   45
Text Books:
1. VNS Murthy (2011), “Text Book of Soil Mechanics and Foundation
Engineering”, CBS Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd,
2. Dr.Alam Singh (2004), “Basic Soil Mechanics and Foundations”, CBS
Publishers and Distributers Pvt. Ltd.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/3
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
Reference Books:
1. Gopal Ranjan& A. S. RAO (2004), “Basic & Applied Soil Mechanics”, New age
international Ltd.
2. Hsai-Yang Fang (2002), “Foundation Engineering Hand Book”, Kluwer
Academic Publishers

1. Minimum seven assignments covering the prescribed syllabus
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/4
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

Pre-requisite: Engineering Mathematics – III (BTAB03001), Strength of Materials
(BTCI03003), Hydraulic Engineering (BTCI04005),
Structural Analysis – I (BTCI04003)
Objectives:
 To introduce concepts and applications of FEM in Engineering problems
 To impart knowledge of one dimensional problems by FEM
 To get acquainted with the analysis of beams, frame and truss problems by
FEM
 To acquire the knowledge of two dimensional problems by FEM
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Describe the basic concept and applications of FEM in Engineering problems
 Solve one dimensional problems by FEM
 Analyze the beam, frame and truss elements by FEM
 Solve two dimensional equations by FEM
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Overview of Finite element analysis:   08
Basic concepts, Types of governing equations, numerical
modelling, General applications of FEM, General description and
comparison with other analysis methods, brief history of FEM,
Merits and demerits of FEM,
2.   Different approaches in FEM:   06
Direct approach, variational, energy and Weighted Residual
approach, Isoparametric elements, Eigen values
3.   One dimensional finite element analysis:   12
1D torsion of a circular shaft, 1D steady state heat conduction, 1D
flow through porous media, 1D ideal flow through pipes, Linear
spring, Flow network analysis, Electrical network analysis
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/5
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

Analysis of beam element, frames and trusses   (based on

approach for two dimensional equations (Laplace, parabolic
equations).

4. 1-D analysis of flow through pipes by FEM
5. Analysis of beam element by FEM
6. Analysis of frames by FEM
7. Analysis of trusses by FEM
8. Solution of two dimensional equations by Galerkin’s method

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester : VI
Course :   Limit State Design of Reinforced Concrete   Code : BTCI06003
Structures
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme

100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   0   2   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Strength of Materials (BTCI03003), Theory of Structures (BTCI05002)
Objectives:
 To impart knowledge of the basic design philosophies of reinforced concrete
structures
 To get acquainted with the limit state method for designing RCC Structures
 To know the basic procedure for designing beams and slabs
 To understand the procedure for designing columns and footings
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Describe basic design philosophies of reinforced concrete structures
 Design the beams of rectangular and flanged sections
 Design simply supported one way, two way and cantilever slabs
 Design columns and isolated column footings subjected to axial loads and
moments
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Ultimate Load Method:   05
Brief introduction to fundamentals of ultimate strength theory:
curved stress distribution, compressive stress block, simplified
rectangular stress block as per Whitney's approach, ultimate
moment of resistance of singly reinforced section and doubly
reinforced sections.
2.   Limit State Method:   04
Introduction to limit state method of design as per IS 456 (latest
edition): concepts of probability and reliability, characteristic
loads, characteristic strength, partial safety factors for loads and
materials, introduction to various limit states.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/7
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Limit State of Collapse - Flexure:   12
Limit state of collapse in flexure, shear and Limit state of
serviceability in deflection and cracking , design of singly and
doubly reinforced rectangular and T sections for flexure, design
of members in shear and bond, design of beam subjected to
bending and torsion. Requirements governing reinforcement
detailing.
4.   Design of Slabs:   06
Design of simply supported one way, two way and cantilever
slabs.
5.   Limit State of Collapse - Compression:   08
Limit state of collapse compression for short and slender column.
Members subjected to combined axial and uni-axial as well as
biaxial bending.
6.   Design of Foundations:   10
Isolated square and rectangular footings subjected to axial load
and moments.
Total   45

Publication, Pune

Structures”, Oxford & IBH

4. H.J. Shah (2008), “Reinforced Concrete Design”, Charotar Publisher
5. Sinha & Roy (2013), “Fundamentals of Reinforced Concrete”, Charotar
Publisher

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester : VI
Course :   Building Utilities and Services   Code : BTCI06004
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous

100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   0   0   3   50   50
Pre-requisite: Building Materials & Construction (BTCI03004)
Objectives:
 To impart the knowledge of the various Building Services & Utilities and their
functions
 To make acquainted with the technical processes involved in building of these
Building Services
 To illustrate the rules and regulations controlling the provisions of these
Building Services
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Identify different Building Services & Utilities required for smooth
functioning of the buildings
 Explain the various Technical Processes involved in building up of these
Building Services
 Discuss the rules and regulations controlling the provisions of these Building
Services
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Lifts and Escalators:   04
Essentials, passenger traffic requirements, incoming, two way
and outgoing traffic. Application to commercial, residential and
institutional buildings.
2.   Plumbing Systems in Building:   09
Plumbing services: Water distribution system, Material for
service, pipes -Service connection-size of service pipe, Water
meter, Valves, Storage tanks.
Drainage system: Pipes and traps, Sanitary fittings, system of
plumbing, House drainage plans, Septic tank, Soak pit.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/9
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Electrical Systems in Buildings:   08
Basics of electricity – Single / Three phase supply, Protective
devices in electrical installations, Earthing for safety, Types of
earthing, IS specifications, Types of wires, wiring systems and
their choice, Planning electrical wiring for building, Main and
distribution boards, Transformers and switch gears, Layout of
substations
4.   Principles of Illumination & Design:   06
Visual tasks, Factors affecting visual tasks, Modern theory of
light and colour, Synthesis of light, Additive and subtractive
synthesis of colour, Luminous flux, Candela, Solid angle
illumination, Utilisation factor, Depreciation factor, MSCP,
MHCP, Laws of illumination, Classification of lighting, Artificial
light sources, Spectral energy distribution, Luminous efficiency,
Colour temperature, Colour rendering, Design of modern
lighting, Lighting for stores, offices, schools, hospitals and house
lighting. Elementary idea of special features required and
minimum   level of illumination required   for physically
handicapped and elderly in building types.

energy efficiency, air filtration and cleaning, Introduction to
HVAC industry standards.

considerations in buildings like non-combustible materials,
construction, staircases and lift lobbies, fire escapes and A.C.
systems. Special features required for physically handicapped
and elderly in building types, Heat and smoke detectors, Fire
alarm system, snorkel ladder, Fire fighting pump and water
storage, Dry and wet risers, Automatic sprinklers.
7.   Miscellaneous Building services:   03
Acoustics and sound insulation: Characteristics of sound, reflection
and absorption coefficient, acoustical defects, design and material
Damp-proofing and water proofing: materials and methods
8.   Introduction to Green Building:   03
Need for a green building, planning and design of green
buildings,   obstacles, Materials used   in green building
technology, Rating System (According to LEED-INDIA)

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester : VI
Course :   Analysis of Structures   Code : BTCI06005
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical Tutorial Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   0   2   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Theory of Structures (BTCI05002).
Objectives:
 To impart knowledge of the behaviour of different structures subjected to
different types of loads
 To evaluate the deformations of the internal forces developed in different
structures under various loads
 To analyse the structures subjected to various loads
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Determine the internal forces developed in various structures subjected to
various loads
 Calculate the deformations in various structures subjected to temperature
change
 Analyse the indeterminate structure by flexibility and stiffness method
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   General:   06
Types of structures occurring in practice and their classification.
Stable and unstable structure, static and kinematic determinacy
and   indeterminacy   of   structure.   Symmetric   structure,
symmetrical and anti-symmetrical loads, distinction between
linear and non-linear behaviour of material and geometric non-
linearity.
2.   Deflection of statically determinate structures:   05
Deflection due to temperature changes, application to beams, pin
jointed frames and rigid jointed frames.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/12
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Analysis of indeterminate structures by flexibility method:   17
Flexibility   coefficients and   their use in formulation of
compatibility   equations.   Theorem   of   three   moments,
Castigliano’s theorem of least work, application of above
methods to propped cantilevers, fixed beams, continuous beams.
Simple pin jointed frames including effect of lack of fit for
members. Simple rigid jointed frames and two hinged parabolic
arches.
4.   Analysis of indeterminate structures by stiffness method:   17
Stiffness coefficients for prismatic members and their use for
formulation of equilibrium equations, direct stiffness method,
slope   deflection method, Moment   distribution method.
Application of the above methods to indeterminate beams and
simple rigid jointed frames, rigid jointed frames with inclined
member but having only one translational degree of freedom in
addition to rotational degree of freedom including the effect of
settlement of supports.
Total   45
Text Book:
1. Reddy C. S. (2007), “Basic Structural Analysis – Second Edition”, Tata
McGraw Hill
Reference Books:
1. G. S. Pandit, S. P. Gupta (2007), “Structural Analysis – A Matrix Approach”,
Tata McGraw Hill
2. John Benson Wilbur, Charles Head Norris (2012), “Elementary Structural
Analysis”, Literary Licensing
3. R. C. Hibbeler (2008), “Structural Analysis – Second Edition”, Pearson
4. Aslam Kassimali (2011), “Matrix Analysis of Structures – Second Edition”,
Cengage Learning

Term work should consists of the following
1. Minimum seven assignments covering the prescribed syllabus

SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester : VI
Course :   Concrete Technology   Code : BTCI06006
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical Tutorial Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   2   0   4   50   50
Pre-requisite: Strength of Materials (BTCI03003)
Building Materials and Construction (BTCI03004)
Objectives:
 To impart the knowledge of properties of the fresh and hardened concrete
 To carry out mix design of concrete
 To study different types of concretes and their ingredients
 To explain different tests for concrete
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Identify the properties of ingredients of concrete and its effect on the
performance of the concrete
 Perform the mix design of concrete.
 Determine different properties of fresh and hardened concrete with the help
of different tests for concrete
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Properties of aggregates:   08
Properties of coarse and fine aggregates and their influence on
concrete, types of cement and their use, physical properties of 33
Grade, 43 Grade, 53 Grade ordinary Portland cement, Portland
Pozzolana   cement,   rapid   hardening   Portland   cement,
hydrophobic cement, low heat Portland cement and Sulphate
Resisting Portland cement as per relevant I.S. codes
2.   Grades of concrete:   07
Concrete for ordinary work, light weight concrete, high density
concrete, workability, durability and strength requirements,
effect of w/c ratio, acceptability criteria, laboratory testing of
fresh and hardened concrete, concreting under special conditions,
work in extreme weather conditions, under-water concreting.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/14
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Concrete mix design:   05
Mix design for compressive strength by I.S. methods, Road Note
method and British method, mix design for flexural strength.
4.   High performance concrete:   05
Constituents of high grade concrete, various tests and application
of high performance concrete.
5.   Admixtures:   05
Plasticizers, retarders, accelerators and other admixtures, test on
admixtures, chemistry and compatibility with concrete.
6.   Ready mix concrete:   05
Requirements of RMC, transit mixer details, mix design of RMC.
7.   Concrete for repairs and rehabilitation of structures:   05
Polymer   concrete,   fiber   reinforced   concrete,   polymer
impregnated   concrete,   polymer   modified   cement
concrete/mortar and ferro-cement, different tests.
8.   Non-Destructive testing of concrete:   05
Hammer test, ultrasonic pulse velocity test, load test, carbonation
test, ½ cell potentiometer test, and corrosion test for steel, core
test and relevant provision of I.S. codes.
Total   45

McGraw Hill
Reference Books:

Hill

3. A. R. Santhakumar (2006), “Concrete Technology”, Oxford University Press
India

2. Report of minimum six experiments performed in the laboratory from the list
given below
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/15
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering

1. Study of properties of fine and coarse aggregates.
2. Physical properties of cement.
3. Effect of w/c ratio on workability (slump cone, compaction factor, V-B test,
flow table)
4. Effect of w/c ratio on strength of concrete
5. Mix design in laboratory
6. Non destructive testing of concrete – some applications (hammer, ultrasonic)
7. Secant modulus of elasticity of concrete & indirect tensile test on concrete.
8. Study of admixtures & their effect on workability and strength of concrete.
9. Modulus of rupture of concrete.
10. Permeability test on concrete.

text:
Program:   B. Tech. (Civil Engineering)   Semester : VI
Course :   Urban and Infrastructure Development   Code : BTCI06007
Teaching Scheme   Evaluation Scheme
Theory   Internal Continuous
Lecture   Practical Tutorial Credit   (3 Hrs,   Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks)   As per Institute Norms
3   0   0   3   50   50
Objectives:
 To introduce economic reforms and infrastructure development
 To get acquainted with the formulation and approval of various
infrastructure projects and financing issues in infrastructure development
 To explain the urban and rural development and town planning
 To introduce the urbanization of cities, suburbs, region and Hinterland
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students should be able to
 Describe Economic Reforms and Infrastructure Development
   Illustrate the Formulation and Approval of Various Infrastructure Projects
and Financing Issues in Infrastructure Development
 Differentiate between Urban and Rural Development and Town Planning
 Discuss urbanization of cities, suburbs, region and Hinterland
Detailed Syllabus:
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Introduction   to Economic Reforms and   Infrastructure   08
Development:
Performance of the States: a review, growth performance,
implications for inter-state inequality, implications for poverty.
The determinants of growth in the states: effect of economic
reforms on regional inequality, investment ratios at the state
level, plan expenditure, human resource and quality of
infrastructure.
Strategy for slow growing states: Development of economic and
social infrastructure, the problem of state finances, the policy
environment and governance, the   role of the Central
Government,
2.   Sectoral Infrastructure Development:   03
Overview, liberalization of FDI regulations, Introduction of
Public Private Partnerships (PPP), Sector Specific Opportunities
for roads, ports, airports, railways, telecommunications, etc.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/17
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
3.   Formulation and Approval of Various Infrastructure Projects   05
based on project cost:
Institutional Structure, Applicability, Project Identification, Inter-
ministerial Consultations, ‘In Principle’ Approval of PPPAC,
Expression of Interest, Formulation of Project Documents,
Appraisal/Approval of PPPAC, Invitation of Bids, Time Frame,
Exemption from the above Procedure
4.   Financing Issues in Infrastructure, Projects Management and   05
Development:
The IIPDF and its role, Background of the IIPDF, The purpose of
the IIPDF, IIPDF funding sources, The IIPDF’s organisational
structure,   Disbursements   by   the   IIPDF,   Operational
management, Funding from IIPDF, Evaluation Procedures and
Timeframe, Monitoring, Recovery of Project Development
Funding with Returns, Risk management
5.   Introduction to Urban Development:   05
Urbanization in India with reference to growth of cities, pattern,
growth its trends, causes and prospects of urbanization, cost of
urbanization, growth of urban population, resources of urban
development, spatial pattern of urbanization, problems of
metropolitan cities in India policy issues and their need, trends
and projections for urbanization.
6.   Integrated Rural and Urban Development:   03
Policy background, Principal rural urban socio-economic
interactions, factors contributing to rural-urban interaction,
effects of economic liberalization policies, recommendations.
7.   Urbanization of Cities, Suburbs, Region and Hinterland:   03
Plans for cities and suburban areas, metropolitan regions, role of
peripheral region in urban development, concept of hinterland,
small towns, tributaries/twin cities of metropolitan cities.
8.   Town Planning:   06
Review of planning legislation and acts relating to urban and
regional planning. Building bye laws planning agencies and their
functions, D.C. rules or city. Concept of FSI, fungible FSI and
TDR. FSI in few important cities across Indian region and around
the World. Norms for FSI utilization for different kind of
buildings like residential, commercial, education and hospitals.
Redevelopment of building in cities. Reforms in D.C rules by U.D
department of state government and municipal authorities.
9.   Notifications :   03
such as CRZ coastal and marine areas, Coastal management
zones, set back line. Norms pertaining to civil aviation for
buildings under funnel.
BTECH/CIVIL/2013-14/SEM VI/18
SVKM'S NMIMS'
Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management and Engineering
10.   Connectivity and conversion:   04
Between Satellite cities, cities of cultural/business/ tourism
attraction, between cities and towns, Cities getting converted into
regions and towns getting converted into cities. Express ways
and freight corridors, Golden Quadrilateral, Hub airport, Impact
of these on urban development.
Total   45
Text Book:
1. V. Nath, S. K. Aggrawal (2007), “Urbanization, Urban Development &
Metropolitan Cities in India”, Concept Publisher
2. Dhameja and Sastry (2002), “Public Sector Restructuring and Privatisation
including Urban Infrastructure and Public Service finance”, Kanishka
Publishers
Reference Books:
1. Savas E.S. (2001), “Privatisation and Public Private Partnerships”, Affiliated
East-West Press Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi
2. D C rules of MCGM latest i.e. (2012), CIDCO and other such bodies
3. Government Notifications pertaining to urban development
4. The Secretariat for the Committee on Infrastructure, Planning Commission,
GOI (2006), “Report of the Core Group; Financing of the National Highway
Development Programme”
Term Work:
Term work should consists of the following
1. Minimum seven assignments covering the prescribed syllabus

excitation
 Analyze the structure using IS code method and response spectrum

loads, different types of dynamic loads, undamped vibration of
SDOF system, natural frequency and periods of vibration,
damping in structure. Response to periodic loads, response to
general dynamic load, response of structure subject to ground
motion, use of Fourier series for periodic forces.

method, IS 1893-2002 provisions for seismic analysis of buildings

Pre-requisite: Knowledge of vector algebra, functions, limits, differentiation and integration of
functions.
Course Objective:
This course aims at providing adequate exposure to the theory and applications of Calculus. This
course will help the students achieve sound understanding of the concepts of calculus, develop
problem solving skills and apply the concepts and techniques of calculus to solve problems within
Engineering domain. This course will equip the students with intermediate to advanced level
concepts and aligned tools to help them tackle advanced mathematics and related applications.
Course Outcomes:
After completion of the course, students will be able to-
1. Demonstrate the fundamental concepts of differential calculus for functions of one variable.
2. Solve problems involving functions of several variables using partial differentiation, Taylor
series expansion, and techniques for finding maxima and minima, including Lagrange’s method
of undetermined multipliers.
3. Use Beta and Gamma functions to solve problems in single-variable calculus.
4. Compute and interpret double and triple integrals, including change of variables and coordinate
transformations, and apply them to determine areas and volumes.
5. Examine vector functions using gradient, divergence, curl, and scalar potential and apply
fundamental vector calculus theorems such as Green’s, Stokes’, and Gauss’ theorems to evaluate
integrals.
6. Integrate concepts from differential, integral, and vector calculus to formulate and solve real-
world problems in physics, engineering, and applied sciences.

1.   Differential Calculus of functions of one variable
Rolle’s theorem, Lagrange’s Mean value theorem, Cauchy’s Mean value   3
theorem
Convergence of Sequences and series, Taylor’s and Maclaurin’s Series   7
Expansion, Indeterminate forms, LHospital's rule.

Pre-requisite: Fundamental knowledge of physics, chemistry, and mathematics.
Course Objective:
To introduce students to modern biology with an emphasis on the evolution of biology as a multi-
disciplinary field, to make them aware of the application of engineering principles in biology. This
will encourage engineering students to think about solving biological problems with engineering
tools. They will also be exposed to the application of engineering principles in biology and
engineering robust solutions inspired by biological examples.
Course Outcomes:
After completion of the course, students will be able to –
1. Identify the principles of biomimicry and explain their applications in engineering and
sustainable design, demonstrating an understanding of biologically inspired solutions. (K1)
2. Classify the fundamental building blocks of life (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic
acids) and describe their structural and functional roles in cellular processes and metabolism.
(K2)
3. Explain the molecular basis of genetic information transfer, including DNA replication,
transcription, and translation, and interpret Mendel's laws and their significance in genetics. (K2)
4. Describe the mechanisms of enzyme action, enzyme-substrate interactions, and enzyme
inhibition, and discuss their industrial and biological applications. (K2)
5. Explain the principles of metabolism and energy transactions, and categorize microorganisms
based on their characteristics, growth kinetics, and applications in biotechnology and drug
discovery. (K1)

Course Objective
This course aims to equip students with practical skills in electronics prototyping and provides hands-on
experience with essential tools, measuring instruments, PCB design, and fabrication techniques.
Additionally, students will gain knowledge in PC hardware assembly, Arduino-based circuit
programming, and aerial robotics, including drone assembly and flight basics.

After completion of the course, the student will be able to -
1. Understand and demonstrate the use of essential hand tools, measuring instruments, and
prototyping equipment for circuit design and testing, (Understand - Level 2)

peripherals, (Understand - Level 2)

real-world applications, (Create- Level 6)

Pre-requisite: Linear Algebra and Ordinary Differential Equations
Course Objective
The principal objective of the course is to develop students' logical reasoning and problem-solving
skills by introducing fundamental concepts of discrete mathematics essential for computer science
and engineering applications. It provides a strong foundation in set theory, logic, combinatorics,
graph theory, and abstract algebra, enabling students to analyze and construct mathematical
arguments. Through the study of proof techniques, recurrence relations, and discrete structures,
students will gain the ability to model computational problems and prove the correctness of
algorithms. The course also highlights the practical applications of discrete mathematics in real-
world contexts, such as data structures, cryptography, network security, and algorithm design,
equipping students for advanced studies and careers in computing.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, students will be able to -
1. Apply fundamental concepts of set theory, relations, and functions to solve mathematical
and computational problems.
2. Construct valid mathematical arguments using propositional and predicate logic, proof
techniques, and induction methods.
3. Analyze combinatorial structures and recurrence relations to model and solve discrete
problems in engineering applications.
4. Implement graph and tree algorithms to solve optimization and network-related problems.
5. Demonstrate an understanding of abstract algebraic structures and their applications in
coding theory.

Course Objective
The course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) by
covering its foundational concepts and advanced applications. Students will gain insight into the
historical development and evolution of RPA, along with a deep appreciation for the benefits and
challenges of its implementation. By delving into RPA tools and their features, students will learn to
harness workflow automation, create apps, grasp the distinctions between attended and unattended
bots, and comprehend the symbiotic relationship between RPA and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

After completion of the course, students will be able to -
1. Demonstrate understanding of fundamental RPA concepts, historical evolution, benefits and
process analysis and selection
2. Analyze RPA tools, design bot workflows, and apply decision-making strategies, constructing
optimized automation processes

workflows, and deploy applications within operational frameworks

implementations, and making informed decisions regarding automation practices
5. Synthesize software bots for operational process automation of practical importance

Course Objective
This course provides the fundamental knowledge of computer networks through understanding each
layer of computer network architecture, and transmission systems to network applications. It also
focuses on congestion control techniques, protocols, and application layer functions.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, students will be able to -
1. Explain the concepts of computer networks, topologies and data communication
2. Analyze the various error detection and correction and medium access techniques
3. Apply network layer addressing and routing techniques to different network topologies
4. Analyze the different protocols of the layered architecture of computer networks

Prerequisite: Software Engineering, Object Oriented Analysis &Design
Course Objective
To understand software quality management process and quality management models. To learn
software quality metrics, assurance and various software standards
Course Outcomes
After completion of this course, student will be able to-
1. Classify the various software quality factors
2. Describe and comprehend SQA architecture and its components
3. Identify the different software defects and techniques used for defects removal
4. Evaluate on the basis of Software quality metrics and the standards
Detailed Syllabus
Unit   Description   Duration
1   Introduction   3
Software quality challenge, software errors, faults and failures, causes of
software errors, software quality and software quality assurance definition.
2   Software quality factors   4
Need for software quality requirements, classification of software
requirements into software quality factors, product operation, revision and
transition software quality factors, alternative models of software quality
factors, software compliance with quality factor.
3   Components of SQA   4
SQA system architecture, pre project software quality components, software
project lifecycle components, infrastructure components for error prevention
and improvement, Management SQA components, SQA standards, system
certification and assessment components, human component.
4   Defect removal effectiveness   4
Software development methodologies, factors affecting QA activities in
development process, Verification, validation and qualification, model for
SQA defect removal effectiveness and cost, reviews.
5   Software testing   4
Definition and objectives, testing process, strategies, software test classification,
black box and white box, test case design, automated testing, Alpha and Beta
site testing programs, Security Testing

Mukesh Patel School of Technology Management & Engineering
6   Maintenance and external participants   5
Pre maintenance software quality components, Maintenance software quality
assurance tools, types of external participants, risks and benefits, assuring
quality of external participants, SQA tools for assuring quality of external
participants
Contribution.
7   Standards   3
Scope of quality management standards, ISO 9001, ISO 9000- 3, CMM and
CMMI, Boot strap methodology, ISO/IEC 15504 model, ISO/IEC 27001
IEEE STD 12207, IEEE STD 1012, IEEE STD 1028.
8   Software quality metrics   3
Objective and classification of software quality metrics, process metrics and
product metrics, implementation and limitation of software quality metrics.
Total   30

Course Objective

covering its foundational concepts and advanced applications. Students will gain insight into the
historical development and evolution of RPA, along with a deep appreciation for the benefits and
challenges of its implementation. By delving into RPA tools and their features, students will learn to
harness workflow automation, create apps, grasp the distinctions between attended and unattended
bots, and comprehend the symbiotic relationship between RPA and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

process analysis and selection

Course Objective
The capstone project is designed to provide a culminating design experience to the final-year
students’ learning with essentially required hands-on experience to ensure that they graduate
with the required practical and soft skills. The course aims to encourage students to think
critically, solve challenging problems, do a feasibility study and develop written and oral
communication skills, teamwork and planning. The students may also work in interdisciplinary
areas which will help broaden their scope and learning in different domains.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, students will be able to -
1. Select an appropriate problem statement after reviewing the literature and identifying the
research gaps.
2. Formulate the different use cases/feasible design model.
3. Implement the prototype/proof of concept, test and validate the results.
4. Manage a team project.
5. Summarize the topic into a technical report.

A student is required to carry out elaborated project work. The project may be either design
and fabrication work or a simulation and synthesis of a problem/system, and develop
algorithms and verify feasibility of implementation. At the end of the semester students will be
required to submit a report detailing the literature review, design problem formulation,
analysis functional simulation and synthesis, work plan and work done and present his/her
work carried out before examiners.

areas which will help broaden their scope and learning in different domains.

research gaps.

algorithms and verify feasibility of implementation. At the end of the semester students will be
required to submit a report detailing the literature review, design problem formulation,

Prerequisite: NA
Course Objective
This course provides the fundamental knowledge of computer networks through
understanding each layer of computer network architecture, and transmission systems to
network applications. It also focuses on congestion control techniques, protocols, and
application layer functions.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, students will be able to -
1. Explain the concepts of computer networks, topologies and data communication.
2. Analyze the various error detection and correction and medium access techniques.
3. Apply network layer addressing and routing techniques to different network
topologies.
4. Analyze the different protocols of the layered architecture of computer networks.
Detailed Syllabus
Unit   Description   Duration
1   Introduction   02
Computer Network, Peer-to-peer and client-server communication,
Classifications of computer networks, Network Topologies.
2   Physical Layer   02
Introduction to OSI and TCP/IP model, Transmission Media.
3   Data Link Layer and Medium Access Sub Layer   07
Fundamentals of Error Detection and Error Correction, Block coding,
Hamming Distance, Flow Control and Error control;   error control
mechanism - CRC; flow control protocols - Stop and Wait ARQ, Go-back–
N ARQ, Selective Repeat ARQ, Multiple access protocols - Random
Access - Pure ALOHA, Slotted ALOHA, CSMA/CD, CDMA/CA.
4   Network Layer   09
Switching techniques, IPV4 addressing, subnet mask, classless inter-
domain routing (CIDR), IPV6; Address mapping – ARP, RARP, and

report detailing the literature review, design problem formulation, analysis functional simulation and

Program: _B. Tech.(Computer Engineering) Semester : VI
Course: Advanced Database Management Code : BTCO06008
System (Elective-I-b)

Teaching Scheme Evaluation Scheme
Theory Internal Continuous
Lecture | Practical | Tutorial | Credit (3 Hrs, Assessment (ICA)
100 Marks) As per Institute Norms
3 2 0 4 Weightage Weightage
60% 40%

Pre-requisite: Database Management System(BTCO03006)

Objectives: Expand on the knowledge gained in Database Management Systems in
several directions like Non-Relational data models, deductive (Intelligent) database
systems, Distributed systems, web based systems and object oriented systems etc.
Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, the students will be able to
1. Design database using concept of extended entity relationship model.
2. Implement functions and procedures using concepts of PL/SQL
3. Implement object oriented concepts in database.
4. Compare and contrast different types of advance database
management systems.
5. Administer and manage the database.
Detailed Syllabus:

Unit | Description Duration
1. The Extended Entity Relationship Model and Object Model: 5

The ER model revisited, Motivation for complex data types, User
defined abstract data types and structured types, subclasses,
super classes, Inheritance, Specialization ‘and Generalization,
Constraints and _ characterisitics of specialization and
generalization, relationship types of degree higher than two.

2. Procedural Language/Structured Query language (PL/SQL): 7
Introduction to PL/SQL, Disadvantages of SQL and advantages
of PL/SQL, PL/SQL block structure, block data types, block
variable declaration, exception handling, Cursors, types of
cursors, functions, procedures, triggers.

3: Object Oriented Databases: Overview of object oriented 5
concepts, object identity, object structure and type constructions,
Encapsulation of operations, Method and persistence, Type
hierarchies and Inheritance, Type extents and queries, Complex
objects; Database schema design for OODBMS; OQL, Persistent
programming language; OODBMS architecture and storage
issues; Transaction and Concurrency control, example of
ODBMS.

4. Object Relational and Extended Relational Databases: Database 4
design for an ORDBMS, Nested relations and collections, storage
and access methods, Query processing and optimization, An
overview of SQL3, Implementation issues of extended type;
System comparison of RDBMS, OODBMS, and ORDBMS.

5. Parallel and Distributed Databases and Client-Server 5
Architecture: Architectures for parallel database, Parallel query
evaluation, Parallelizing individual operations, Sorting, Joins,
Distributed Database Concepts, Data Fragmentation, Replication,
and allocation techniques for distributed database design; Query
processing in distributed databases; Concurrency control and
Recovery in distributed databases. An overview of Client-Server
architecture.

6. Databases on the web and Semi-Structured Data: Web 5
interfaces of the web. Overview of XML; data XML applications;

The semi structured data model, Implementation issues, Indexes
for data.

7. Enhanced data models for Advanced applications: Active 7
database concepts, Temporal database concepts, Spatial database
concepts and architecture, Deductive databases and Query
processing, Mobile databases, Geographic information systems.

8. Database Administration: Managing a database instance, 7
Maintaining an Online Redo Log files, Managing table spaces
and data files, Managing undo data, Managing users and
privileges, Managing roles and auditing.

Total 45
Text Books:
Elmarsi, Navathe, Fundamentals of Database Systems, 5'* edition, Addison Wesley,

2006
Reference Books:
1. Stefano Ceri and Giuseppe Pelagatti, Distributed Databases Principles and
Systems, McGraw Hill, 1985.
2. R.Ramakrishnan, Database Management Systems, 34 edition, McGraw Hill,
2002
3. Hennery Korth, Abraham Silberschatz, Database System Concepts, 5th
edition, McGraw Hill, 2005.
4. Bipin Desai, An Introduction to Database System, Galgotia.
5. CJ. Date, An Introduction to Database System, 8'h edition, Addison Wesley,
2003
6. W. Kim, Modern Database System, ACM Press, Addison Wesley, 1995.
7. George Koch, Oracle 8i - The complete Reference, Tata McGraw Hill, 2001
8. Ivan Bayross, Oracle Developer 2000, BPB.

Term Work: As per Internal Continuous Assessment (ICA) norms of the institute
No of Practicals: 15
No of Assignments: 02 or more

Pre-requisite: Operating System (BTCO04003)

Objectives:
e This course provides introduction of Unix Structure, Architecture,

Commands, file structure, different message passing techniques and related
programming.

Outcomes:
After successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. Analyze UNIX architecture and utilize different commands and utilities of
UNIX.

2. Identify, analyze and implement mechanisms like file system, Processes,
Signals and Threads in UNIX.

3. Analyze and implement Inter process communication in UNIX using various
methods.

4. Identify and recognize the importance of Terminal Input-Output methods
and Operating system design functions and parameters

5. Understand the comparison of the UNIX operating system with Windows
operating system and Identify different UNIX versions / releases.

Detailed Syllabus:
Unit | Description Duration
1. Unix System Overview: Unix Architecture, Traditional Modern, 6

Feature of Unix, Commands, General purpose Utilities, System
Calls, Standardization, File I/O.

2. File Handling in Unix: The file system, Handling Ordinary Files, 6
File Attributes, Ownership, Permission, ‘Inodes, Links, File
System Calls, Standard I/O Library, System data files and
information.

3. Process in Unix: The process environment, PCB, Process state 7
diagram, Process Relationships, Process Creation, Running,
Process termination, Killing Process, Daemon Processes.
4. Signals and Threads: Introduction, Signal Concept, Unreliable 7
signals, Reentrant function, Reliable signal terminology and
semantics, signal sets, Thread: creation, termination.

5. Interprocess Communication: Introduction of Message passing 7
and Shared Memory Technology, Pipes, Co-processors, Network
IPC: Sockets, STREAMS Based Pipes, Unix Domain Sockets,
Passing File descriptors.

6. Terminal I/O: Introduction, Terminal Option Flags, Baud rate 4
functions, Line control functions, Terminal Identification:
Canonical mode, non-canonical mode.

7 Operating System Design: The nature of design functions, Line 5
control functions, Terminal Identification, Performance, Project
Management, Trends in Operating System Design.

8 Case Study: 1. Comparison of UNIX and WINDOWS 3

2. Various Unix releases i.e. Ubuntu, Fedora.

Total 45

Text Books:
1. W. Richard Stevens, Stephen A.Rago, Advanced Programming in the Unix

Environment’, 2"4 edition, Pearson Education, 2009.

Reference Books:

1. Sumitabha Das, “Unix and Shell Programming”, Tata Mc Graw Hill, 2008.

2. Sumitabha Das, “Unix concepts and Applications”, Tata Mc Graw Hill (374
Edition) (2010).

3. William Stallings, “Operating Systems: Internals and Design Principles”, PHI
Publication (5 Edition) (2012)

4. Andrew S.Tanenbaum, “Operating Systems”, PHI publications (24
Edition)(2011)

Term work consists of the following:
1. Minimum 10 practicals.

2. Two term tests.
3. Minimum three Assignments

3. Perform Project scheduling using PERT and CPM techniques with uncertain

appreciate the aims to study sequencing techniques.

Unit | Description Duration

Characteristics of OR, Necessity of OR in industry, OR and
decision making, Role of computers in OR.

Graphical Method, Simplex Method, Big-M Method, Two Phase

Gomory’s Cutting Plane Method, Branch and Bound Method.
06

Restricted), Travelling Salesman Problem.

Introduction, Critical Path Analysis (CPM), Project Scheduling
with uncertain activity times (PERT).

06

6. Queuing Theory: 04
Introduction, Features of queuing system, queuing models-

Course Objectives
This course aims to introduce basic concepts of probability theory and calculus. The course
will equip the students with intermediate to advanced level concepts in probability and
statistics using calculus tools that will help them to tackle relevant
problems within engineering domain.
Course Outcomes

1. explain the basic concepts of differential and integral calculus, statistical data,
probability and random variables,
2. solve problems involving conditional probability, moments and various
probability distributions, differential and integral calculus,
3. apply knowledge of various probability distributions, measures of central
tendency, differential and integral calculus to evaluate real life problems,
4. demonstrate use of differential and integral calculus in probability theory.

Course Objective
The course aims to apply electrical circuit fundamentals to the AC and DC circuits and study
electromagnetism. The course also intends to focus on understanding the concept and working of
the transformer, measuring devices, and sensors. The course concludes with a case study
discussion of IoT applications.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, students will be able to -
1. Explain DC network theorems and apply them to solve DC circuits
2. Understand AC fundamentals and use them to solve AC circuits
3. Understand the operating principle of the transformer
4. Describe various measuring devices and sensors
5. Understand the application of computer science and electrical engineering principles in
real-time application
Detailed Syllabus
Unit   Description   Duration
1   Introduction to DC Circuit Fundamentals
Definitions: Electrical Potential and Potential Difference, Current, Work,
Power and Energy, Active and Passive Elements and Circuits, Linear and
Non-linear Elements and Circuits, Unilateral and Bilateral Elements and
Circuits.
Network Elements: Ohm's Law, Resistance and its Properties, Concept of
Series and Parallel Connection in Network, Series and Parallel
Connection of Resistors, Concept of Voltage Division and Current
Division, Capacitance, Dielectric Capacitor, Composite Dielectric
Capacitors, Series and Parallel Connection of Capacitors, Energy Stored   06
in Capacitors, Charging and Discharging of capacitors (Transient
Analysis), Self and Mutual Inductance, Series and Parallel Connection of
Inductor, Energy Stored in Inductor, Charging and Discharging of
Inductor (Transient Analysis).
Energy Sources: Ideal and Practical Voltage and Current Sources, Concept
of Dependent and Independent Sources (Definitions only for dependent
or controlled sources).

Only)

Generation of 1-phase AC Signal

Peak Factor
Concept of Leading and Lagging AC Quantities
12
Analysis of R, L, C, RL, RC, RLC Series Circuit, RLC Parallel Circuit,
Phasor Representation in Polar and Rectangular Form, Concept of
Impedance, Admittance, Active, Reactive, Apparent and Complex Power,
Power Factor

mathematical techniques

Course Objective
The course would enable students to get a brief introduction of the Indian Constitution and
its principles. The students would have knowledge of concept of   ‘State’ and
interdependencies of its institutions vis a vis their relation with fundamental rights.
Course Outcomes
After completion of the course, students will be able to-
1. Understand the historic evolution of the Indian Constitution, its drafting, nature and
to understand the principles mentioned in its Preamble
2. Inculcate fundamental rights in its true sense and also the permissible restrictions
upon it so as to enjoy these rights within permissible limits while simultaneously
performing their duties and to apply these principles into their professional lives
3. Ingrain the structure of our polity and role of Judiciary in maintaining the basic
structure of the Constitution
4. Attain knowledge of the Emergency provisions, when and how it is imposed, to know
the additional powers the bestowed upon the Government at times of Emergency and
to understand the Amendment procedure
Detailed Syllabus
Unit   Description   Duration
1.   Nature, Characteristics and Sources of Indian Constitution   02
2. Fundamental rights and Fundamental duties – Concept of State,
Right to Equality under Articles 14 and 15, Right to certain   06
freedoms under Article 19, Right to Life and liberty under Article
21, Right to religion under Article 25 and 26, Right to remedy
under Article 32 and Fundamental duties

Course Objectives

identify and implement appropriate data structure and determine the

Course Outcomes
